title: Why musicians left New Orleans for Chicago
summary: Punch says he sought money, and Oliver's letters drew others north.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. How come you left New Orleans to go to Chicago?

Well, I think it just was the idea of, I was after a little money. I wasn't making enough anything. People were all bragging about how people from here was going to Chicago, doing good, in New York, cleaning up, making big money, and I just thought I'd get on up there and make some of it too, which I did. I did.
What was the main reason for people leaving the South in those days? Leaving New Orleans?

Well, my idea was, take a fellow like Joe Oliver, one of them who left first, and they were just writing back, telling the other guys how good it was up there, you know, and going on like that, and first thing you know, another one, he done left, and later on, and the others done left, and they all just went up there and started making goods, see. That's how it happened.
And that's just, just the way all that went.
